prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity restrained dark desktop personal portfolio comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design the familiar contemporary developer portfolio for Colton Spurgin, executed with the direct biography and content density of Lee Robinson, the sticky context and scannable experience list of Brittany Chiang, and the quiet interaction craft of Rauno Freiberg. Benchmark their clarity and finish without copying any one site.
Scene/backdrop: flat front-facing website screenshot on dark navy-black
Subject: Colton is a software developer, Air Force NCO, research assistant, and UWF senior studying artificial intelligence; he graduates December 2026
Style/medium: polished contemporary dark portfolio, clean sans-serif, quiet teal accent, subtle hover states, excellent spacing and accessibility
Composition/framing: a sticky left column contains “Colton Spurgin”, “Software developer · Air Force NCO · Research assistant”, and the plain paragraph “I’m a senior at UWF studying artificial intelligence. I graduate in December 2026 and plan to pursue a master’s degree.” Add text links About, Experience, Work and GitHub, LinkedIn, Email. A scrolling right column shows About with a short factual paragraph, Experience as three simple rows for Lead software developer intern, Air Force NCO, Research assistant, then Selected work as four restrained text-and-thumbnail rows for Bork, VeLLM, Traveling Salesman benchmarks, and Home lab. No promotional calls to action.
Color palette: navy black #0b1220, cool white #d5dde8, slate #8996a8, muted teal #64a8a0
Materials/textures: clean dark field, soft hover wash, small real-project thumbnail placeholders, hairline dividers
Text (verbatim): “Colton Spurgin”; “Software developer · Air Force NCO · Research assistant”; “I’m a senior at UWF studying artificial intelligence. I graduate in December 2026 and plan to pursue a master’s degree.”; “About”; “Experience”; “Work”; “GitHub”; “LinkedIn”; “Email”; “Lead software developer intern”; “Air Force NCO”; “Research assistant”; “Selected work”; “Bork”; “VeLLM”; “Traveling Salesman benchmarks”; “Home lab”
Constraints: ordinary language; normal-size headings; clearly usable and polished dark website; no slogan, no logo, no portrait, no invented employer names, metrics, awards, testimonials, or research specifics
Avoid: marketing landing page, oversized hero type, visual metaphor, themed interface, bento grid, neon, cyberpunk, terminal UI, cockpit, glassmorphism, gradients, decorative illustrations, excessive rounded cards, 3D mockup, browser chrome, watermark
